$comment: xf's own, in bigquery-functions.json's format: the operators written as a call after a table in FROM. The editor offers them there alone, not where a function goes.

functions.name: PIVOT
functions.doc: Turns rows into columns: a column for each value of `input_column`, holding the aggregate of the rows with that value, grouped by the table's other columns. It goes after a table or a subquery in FROM.

params.name: aggregate
params.doc: an aggregate of one column, as SUM(sales); several need a prefix each, which begins their columns' names (total_Q1)

params.name: input_column
params.doc: the column whose values become columns

params.name: values
params.doc: the values that become columns, each a constant, as ('Q1', 'Q2'); a column is named for its value ('Q1' gives Q1, 1 gives _1) unless AS names it

signatures.returns: the other columns, and a column for each value

notes: Aggregates that ignore NULL only, and COUNT; each takes one argument.
The columns the aggregates and `input_column` read are not in the result; every other column groups it, so select only the columns you need in a subquery first.

example.sql: SELECT * FROM (SELECT product, quarter, sales FROM t) PIVOT(SUM(sales) FOR quarter IN ('Q1', 'Q2'))

functions.name: UNPIVOT
functions.doc: Turns columns into rows: a row for each of the columns listed, `values_column` holding its value and `name_column` its name. It goes after a table or a subquery in FROM.

params.name: values_column
params.doc: the name of the new column that holds the values; (a, b) for several, with column sets in IN

params.name: name_column
params.doc: the name of the new column that holds which column each value came from

params.name: columns
params.doc: the columns to turn into rows, all of one type; a label, a string or an INT64, goes in name_column in place of the column's name

signatures.returns: the other columns, values_column and name_column

notes: Rows whose value is NULL are left out; `UNPIVOT INCLUDE NULLS (...)` keeps them.

example.sql: SELECT * FROM t UNPIVOT(sales FOR quarter IN (Q1, Q2))
